page.layout: Two printed pages on the scan. Left page: a narrow strip of small, cramped margin notes along its outer edge, mostly illegible. Right page: one column of glossary entries (Greek and Hebrew names with Latin glosses) under the head number at top right; no running head; signature mark at the foot.

main_text.p: ᾿Ιεριχὼ ἡ nomen urbis ἀκλιῶν, Heb. Lunæ urbs. olim dicta fuit urbs palmarum Deut.34.3. Jud.1.16.
᾿Ιερεμίας ὁ nomen prophetæ, Hebr. exaltans DOMINUM.
᾿Ιεροσόλυμα ἡς ἡ, Matth.2.3. καὶ ἱεροσόλυμα ὧν τὰ, καὶ ἱερουσαλὴμ ἡ ἀκλιῶν, nomen metropolis, Hebr. metuite Schalemum.
᾿Ιεχωνίας ὁ nomen viri, Hebr. præparatus à DOMINO.
᾿Ιλυρικὸν τὸ nomen regionis, ita dicta ab Illyrico Cadmi filio, ut tradit Eusthadius.
᾿Ιορδάνης ὁ nomen fluvii, Hebr. orientis ex Jor & Dan, qui sunt duo fontes ad radices Libani.
᾿Ιουνίας ὁ nomen viri, Latin.Derivatur à nomine Junius, qui mensis a junioribus dictus fuit, sicut Majus à majoribus.

page.notes: Left page margin notes are too small, cramped and damaged to read; not transcribed. Greek headwords are read from a small, heavily inked scan and several accents and breathings are uncertain; the Greek letters may contain errors. The first entry's Greek word and the Greek forms in the Hebrew-name entries are doubtful. The Greek in the entry "᾿Ιεροσόλυμα" and "᾿Ιεροσολυμίτης" is only approximate.
